1. (Currently amended) A method comprising: determining, by a processor, that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; accessing, by the processor, a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; receiving, by the processor, an indication from the data store that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication with respect to at least one of the payment transactions; accepting, by the processor, the received indication as proof-of-life with respect to the recipient; and making, by the processor, the benefit payment to the recipient in response to said proof-of-life, wherein the method is performed by an automated computer system and is not a mental process or abstract idea standing alone.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said at least one payment transaction occurred during a pre-determined period of time prior to said accessing step, and wherein the method is performed by an automated computer system configured to access and process transaction records stored in a computer database.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said pre-determined period of time is seven days.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said pre-determined period of time is 24 hours.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment, and wherein the method is performed by an automated computer system that processes government benefit payments.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the at least one of the payment transactions includes a credit card account transaction and/or a debit card account transaction, and wherein the method is performed by an automated computer system that accesses payment transaction records from financial institutions.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 6, wherein a mobile device was used by the recipient to initiate the at least one payment transaction, and wherein the processor accesses transaction records indicating biometric authentication performed on the mobile device.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is made via an electronic monetary transfer to an account owned by the recipient, and wherein the processor executes the electronic transfer through a financial network.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the benefit payment is made by sending a check to the recipient, and wherein the processor initiates a check printing and mailing process through an automated system.

10. (Currently amended) A method comprising: determining, by a processor, that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; accessing, by the processor, at a first point in time, a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; determining, by the processor, that the data store contains an indication that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication most recently with respect to one of said payment transactions at a second point in time earlier than the first point in time; comparing, by the processor, a time interval defined by the second and first points in time with a pre-determined permissive time interval; making, by the processor, the benefit payment, without requiring proof-of-life authentication of the recipient, in a case where the time interval defined by the second and first points in time does not exceed the pre-determined permissive time interval; and requiring, by the processor, proof-of-life authentication of the recipient, prior to making the benefit payment, in a case where the time interval defined by the second and first points in time exceeds the pre-determined permissive time interval, wherein the method is performed by an automated computer system and is not a mental process or abstract idea standing alone.

11. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10, wherein the pre-determined permissive time interval is seven days, and wherein the processor automatically compares the time interval to determine whether to require additional authentication.

12. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10, wherein the pre-determined permissive time interval is 24 hours, and wherein the processor automatically compares the time interval to determine whether to require additional authentication.

13. (Currently amended) The method of claim 10, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment, and wherein the processor is part of an automated government benefit payment system.

14. (Original) An apparatus comprising: a processor; and a memory in communication with the processor, the memory storing program instructions, the processor operative with the program instructions to perform functions as follows: determining that a benefit payment is due to be made to a recipient; accessing a data store containing records of payment transactions made by the recipient; receiving an indication from the data store that the recipient had successfully performed a biometric user authentication with respect to at least one of the payment transactions; accepting the received indication as proof-of-life with respect to the recipient; and making the benefit payment to the recipient in response to said proof-of-life.

15. (Original) The apparatus of claim 14, wherein said at least one payment transaction occurred during a pre-determined period of time prior to said accessing.

16. (Original) The apparatus of claim 15, wherein said pre-determined period of time is seven days.

17. (Original) The apparatus of claim 15, wherein said pre-determined period of time is 24 hours.

18. (Original) The apparatus of claim 14, wherein the benefit payment is a social insurance transfer payment.

19. (Original) The apparatus of claim 14, wherein the at least one of the payment transactions includes a credit card account transaction and/or a debit card account transaction.

20. (Original) The apparatus of claim 19, wherein a mobile device was used by the recipient to initiate the at least one payment transaction.
